_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: Once the user edits a chat from the bookmarklet, what they pick goes into its draft too. Call "drafts" lists the text of each draft the server keeps ("none" when there are none). The test opens Shelley from the bookmarklet as a user would: it takes the bookmarklet from Shelley, then clicks it on a page on another origin, http://host.test/ (title "Host Page", a main with an h1 "Host Page", a paragraph #para "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog." and a list ul.list of "First item" and "Second item"), with that paragraph selected. The bookmarklet adds a toolbar to the host page, the element "shelley-bookmarklet", whose controls are in its open shadow root: a status span ".status" and the buttons Record, Pick, Shelley and Close. It opens Shelley in a popup, tab "popup", "the Shelley window". "The toolbar status" is the ".status" element in the toolbar: {"within": {"selector": "shelley-bookmarklet"}, "selector": ".status"} (selectors reach into open shadow roots, but a combinator like "shelley-bookmarklet .status" does not cross into one). Pick the toolbar's buttons by role "button" and exact accessible name, also with "within" the toolbar. Opening it: 1. Navigate to /new. 2. Click the button whose accessible name contains "More options". 3. The overflow menu's bookmarklet item is the bookmarklet too: keep its link, which must be a javascript: URL, with eval (window.__href = document.querySelector('[data-testid=bookmarklet-menu-item]')?.getAttribute('href') ?? '').startsWith('javascript:') expecting true. 4. Click [data-testid="bookmarklet-menu-item"], which opens a dialog with the bookmarklet to drag. 5. That dialog's link has the same href: eval document.querySelector('[data-testid=bookmarklet-link]')?.getAttribute('href') === window.__href expecting true. Then hand the link to the host page with eval fetch('http://host.test/bookmarklet', { method: 'POST', body: window.__href }).then((r) => r.ok) expecting true. Navigate tab "host" to http://host.test/. In tab "host", select the paragraph: eval getSelection().selectAllChildren(document.getElementById('para')). In tab "host", click the bookmarklet as if in the bookmarks bar: eval fetch('/bookmarklet').then((r) => r.text()).then((href) => { location.href = href; }). In tab "host", the toolbar status should be visible with exactly the text "Linked". Then perform these steps in order: 1. In the Shelley window, [data-testid="message-input"] must have the value exactly {{PAGE}}. 2. In the Shelley window, click the message input, press Control+End, and type " Why?". 3. In tab "host", click the toolbar's "Pick" button, then click the page's h1. 4. In the Shelley window, the message input's value must be exactly {{EDITED}}. 5. Call "drafts" should come to return exactly {{EDITED}}.
